fields.default: We don't treat kindness as a feeling. We treat it as infrastructure — something you can plan, staff, budget and measure.

fields.label: Who we are — text
fields.default: True Kind Foundation works with underserved communities on the things that most reliably change a household's trajectory: a usable skill, an income a woman controls, a daughter who stays in school, a neighbourhood with clean air and shade. We keep the program list short on purpose — five things done properly beat fifteen done at a glance.

Kindness, run like an institution. — intro paragraph
fields.default: Good intentions don't help anyone until somebody follows through on them. Here's who we are, why we started, and what we hold ourselves accountable for.

fields.label: Why we exist — text
fields.default: True Kind Foundation began with a plain observation: most communities aren't short on people willing to help. They're short on organisations that convert that willingness into something still standing after the first visit.

fields.label: Why we exist — text
fields.default: So we built ours around follow-through. A skilling batch isn't finished when the certificates are handed out — it's finished when we know whether the graduate found work. A health camp isn't a one-day event — it's the doorway into a community we intend to keep showing up for.

fields.label: Why we exist — text
fields.default: We keep the program list short by design: skill development, women's empowerment, digital education, health & safety, and environmental sustainability. Five things done properly beat fifteen done at a glance.

fields.label: Five programs, chosen for how they compound. — intro paragraph
fields.default: A trained young person earns. An earning mother keeps her daughter in school. A school with a working computer lab produces the next trainee. We picked these five because each one makes the other four go further.

fields.label: Skill Development & Employment — text
fields.default: Trade and digital-service training designed around what employers within travelling distance are actually hiring for. Batches run year-round; placement support continues for six months after the certificate, because that's when most people quietly fall out of the system.

fields.label: Women's Empowerment — text
fields.default: Savings collectives, micro-enterprise training and the unglamorous part nobody funds — market linkages. Products only pay if there's a buyer, so we work on pricing, bulk supply and retailer introductions alongside the skills themselves.

fields.label: Digital Education Access — text
fields.default: Device-light computer and internet literacy labs run alongside government schools. Low hardware requirements on purpose — a lab that needs constant power and new machines is a lab that stops running by year two.

fields.label: Health & Safety Camps — text
fields.default: Preventive-care camps, workplace safety training and first-aid literacy for communities a long way from the nearest clinic. Screening catches the conditions that are cheap to manage early and ruinous to treat late.

fields.label: Environmental Sustainability — text
fields.default: Neighbourhood tree-planting, plastic-reduction drives and environment education, co-run with residents. Saplings are counted at planting and again a year later — survival rate is the number that matters, not the number in the ground.

fields.label: A note from our Chairperson. — text
A note from our Chairperson. — section label
A note from our Chairperson. — heading (H1)
Page — text
fields.default: Dear friend of True Kind Foundation,

fields.label: Page — text
fields.default: Every program on this website started as someone's small decision to show up — a volunteer who kept coming back, a donor who asked hard questions before writing a cheque, a family who let us into their neighbourhood before we'd earned any right to be there. None of what we do works without that first, ordinary act of trust.

fields.label: Page — text
fields.default: I want to be honest about what we are: not a large institution, not a finished project, but a group of people trying to do a few things properly rather than many things loosely. We measure what we can. We say plainly when something hasn't worked. We ask for help when we need it. That's the whole method.

fields.label: Page — text
fields.default: If you're reading this while deciding whether to volunteer, donate, or simply trust us with your time — thank you for taking that decision seriously. We don't take it lightly either. Kindness, in our experience, is the easy part. Organising it, sustaining it, and being accountable for it is the actual work, and it's the work we've committed ourselves to.
